A snapjaw closed on you. It had been waiting all day.
[dryly] Eaten by the shrubbery. The Rot Gardens are not decorative.
You were felled.
A tree fell in the Works, and someone was around to hear it. Briefly.
[dryly] Timber. The creak was, in hindsight, the warning.
[nervous] Oh! Oh, thank goodness. You’re a person. Sorry. I’ve been talking to a duck all week.
Pell. Guild surveyor. I came down a year ago to finish the map, and I have very nearly finished being frightened.

Pell. Guild surveyor. I came down a year ago to finish the map, and I have very nearly finished being frightened.
[softly] Come in, little breath. We are the Old Ones. We were the Guild, once. Now we are what the Works kept.
[softly] Come in, little breath. We are the Old Ones. We were the Guild, once. Now we are what the Works kept.
[softly] Come in, little breath. We are the Old Ones. We were the Guild, once. Now we are what the Works kept.
[softly] Come in, little breath. We are the Old Ones. We were the Guild, once. Now we are what the Works kept.
The Bellows again. They remember you. I would not take it personally.
The creatures were not in the Guild’s plans. Then again, neither was most of what happened after.
The Bellows. The lungs of the Works. They have breathed for a hundred years, and never once asked permission.
Mind the duck. I say it every time, and it has never once been unnecessary.
The Warm Refuge. Sit a while. The Works have always been kinder to those who sit still.
The Guild built the Tea Engine to settle an argument. Nobody remembers the argument. The tea was excellent.
The lamps never reached the Undertow. The Guild called it thrift. I call it an oversight with a view.
Down you go. You know the way. So, I suspect, does the way.
The Lower Bell. Every floor below is hungrier than this one. Carry the bell; the gates still answer to it.
[softly] The Bellows. The evening the Guild sealed them.
[softly] Everyone went up the lift that night. Nearly everyone.
[softly] We closed the valves by hand. The Works breathed out, and would not breathe in again.
[softly] Someone had to stay and write it all down. I volunteered. It seemed the polite thing.
The Rot Gardens. Everything grows, and all of it burns. I’ll go ahead and mark the safe ways.
Glowseeds. Throw one, and everything hungry looks at it instead of you.
[laughs] Ha! No. I mean, I’d only slow you down. I’ll meet you further down. I’m very good at further down.
Mind the duck!
Strange. I feel as though I’ve told you all this already.
[surprised] Oh! It’s you. Isn’t it? You’ve got the look. The I’ve-done-this-before look.
Rot Gardens. Flammable. I go ahead. I’m starting to think the Works keep sending you back.
Always. Here. Throw them at anything with teeth.
See you further down!
I’ve started leaving the kettle on for you.
Already in your satchel. I’m getting good at this.
Further down!
You again! Right. Rot Gardens, flammable, I go ahead, you save the day. Same as always.
The Gardens have grown since your last visit. It is their only hobby.
The Bellows. Breathes every ninety seconds, like clockwork, because it is clockwork. The duck is in charge.
The Rot Gardens. The gut of the Works, where the Guild’s leftovers learned to grow. Everything here is food, or hoping to be.
Marsh gas gathers under the ceilings. It is perfectly harmless, right up until it is the opposite.
[softly] A year ago. A surveyor, coming down, with a lantern on a pole and a great deal of paper.
Somewhere down here the Old Ones keep their beds. Tread softly. They tread softly around yours.
[softly] He was frightened of nearly everything. He came down anyway.
[softly] I did try to send him home. He was very polite about not listening.
[relieved] You made it! I was worried. I’m always worried, but specifically about you.
The air’s thicker down here. The Old Ones say the Works are holding their breath.
[whispers] There’s a room sealed up behind the rot. I’ve marked it on your compass. Don’t tell the Old Ones I peeked.
Cisterns next. Bring a towel. I didn’t.
This page was stuck in a mushroom. I can’t read it. You look like someone who can.
Marked. Same as last time, probably.
There you are. I kept a path clear for you. Mostly clear. Some of it is on fire.
Another page. The mushrooms keep eating them. Take it before they do.
Cisterns next. Towel!
Still cold. The milk, I am told, is still perfectly fine.
The Rot Gardens. Do not light anything. Do not light anything at all. I lit something.
The Cold Store. The Guild kept the Works’ temper here, in ice. Also the milk.
Everything down here keeps. Food, water, grudges. Keep moving, and you will not join them.
[softly] The Cold Store, on its last day. The ice for the Heart went down in blocks, on trolleys.
[softly] The final delivery never left. It is still here, perfectly preserved. So is the clerk’s temper.
[nervous] It’s freezing. I’ve lost the feeling in two fingers and one of my opinions.
Everything in here keeps. Let’s not be one of the things it keeps.
There’s a locker nobody’s opened in years. I’ve marked it.
See you further down. Somewhere warmer, please.
A frozen page. Thaw it gently. It might be a spell, or a very old grocery list.
Still cold. Still here. Still slightly worried about you.
Marked it. Mind the ice.
Somewhere warmer next!
Frozen page. Same as always. Thaw gently.
The Cold Store. Everything keeps. It kept my sandwich for a year. I did not eat it.
The Cisterns carried the Works’ water, once. Now the water carries itself, and a good deal else besides.
Still wet, I’m afraid. It is a cistern. We did try.
Water carries a current. So will you, if you are careless with a spark. Stand somewhere dry, and be clever.
[softly] The Cisterns, on the morning the Heart missed its first beat.
The thing in the sump was a pump, originally. I suspect it has forgotten. I suspect it is happier that way.
[softly] Then the Works coughed, and the water ran the wrong way. We took that as a sign.
[softly] Every pipe in the Works went quiet at once. For a moment, you could hear the town above.
[nervous] I went down to the sump. I saw it. The Leviathan. I did not scream. Much.
It hates the dry. Drain its pool, and it’s only a very large, very cross fish.
Behind the old valves there’s a room nobody’s opened. It’s marked.
It was floating. Pages float, you know. It’s the only thing down here that does.
[warmly] My last tin of tea. No, take it. Don’t argue. You need it more than I do.
The sump again. Drain it, remember? You do remember. You’ve got the look.
I’m going on to the Kiln. Someone has to map it. Don’t worry about me. I’ve got a lantern.
Marked. Behind the valves, as ever.
A floating page. Dry it off.
Tea. Take it. I insist, every time.
Kiln next. I’ll go ahead. I always go ahead.
The glass remembers you. Try not to squint at it.
The Cisterns. Wet. A large tenant in the sump. Its pool drains through the floor, if you are brave.
The Glass Galleries. The Guild ground its lenses here, to watch the Heart. The glass, it turns out, watched back.
Light behaves oddly in the Galleries. It has had a great deal of time to practise.
[softly] The Glass Galleries, on the day the Great Lens was finished.
[softly] Nobody wrote down what else it showed. I did ask.
[softly] Everyone stopped work to look through it. It showed the Heart, beating.
The glass hums when the Heart beats. It’s humming faster.
[nervous] Don’t look at your reflection too long. It starts looking back. I’m fairly sure that’s not normal.
There’s a gallery behind the mirrors. I’ve marked it. Don’t make eye contact.
This page was under a lens. The writing moves. Good luck.
[warmly] My last tin of tea. Take it. The glass doesn’t drink.
The glass remembers you. I do too, somehow.
Kiln next. I’ll go ahead. The glass says I shouldn’t. I’m ignoring the glass.
Behind the mirrors. Marked.
A moving page. Hold it still.
Tea. Take it.
Kiln next. Ahead, as always.
The Glass Galleries. The light bends, and so does your sense of direction. Follow the humming.
The Heart remembers you. It has been counting.
The Kiln Heart. Listen. That beat is not yours. It is slower than yours, and it is failing.
Its stoker is still at its post. It was always the most loyal thing down here. That is rather the difficulty.
When it heaves, climb. You know this. I simply enjoy saying it.
When the Heart stops fighting, it will heave, and everything below will come up to meet you. When it does: climb.
[softly] The Kiln, a hundred years ago. The Guild’s first stoker, on its very first morning.
[softly] When the Heart began to fail, it would not leave it. It still hasn’t.
[softly] It was built to shovel coal, and not to think. It thought anyway. Mostly about coal.
[softly] Be kind to it, if you can. It is only doing its job.
[softly] The Kiln. The stoker is sad, I think. Don’t tell anyone I said that.
The old flue goes up from the Heart. I’m going to make sure it’s open. See you at the top. P.
Gone ahead again. Flue, top, see you there. P. P.S. The stoker is still sad.
The sump. You remember the way it looks at you.
The sump. It was a pump, once. It has not been one for a very long time.
[urgently] The Heart is heaving. Up, apprentice! The flue! Now!
The Kiln, and its stoker, still at its post after all these years. Go gently. It will not.
The Kiln. It has kept the fire in for you.
Nearly there. I can hear the town.
[urgently] Up! You know the way!
[dryly] Do not look down. It is only lava. It is only everything.
[dryly] Guild regulations forbid that, strictly. The Guild, however, is not here.
